Plock New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Płock, Poland

Not demolished. Established in 1845 (see the Płock Old Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history), this cemetery originally covered about 3.7 hectares before WWII. Both German occupiers and some local residents devastated the site during and after the war. A 1946 funeral reburied 25 people shot by Germans at Imielnica in 1940, exhumed from their original mass grave; a 1949 monument by Beniamin Perelmuter marked the site. The Social and Cultural Society of Jews in Poland maintained the cemetery through the 1960s. In 1964, city officials proposed removing the mass-grave monument due to poor condition and closure plans; it was demolished in 1967, replaced by a new Lucjan Kot-designed monument at decade's end. 1981-1982 discussions between the Jewish Religious Union and city authorities addressed transferring cemetery administration to the city.
